title: An unconfigured pool is inert: missing slippage or TWAP settings revert rather than fall back to a default
content:
Three distinct revert reasons in this chunk exist purely to reject *absent* configuration: `CurveLib/max-slippage-not-set` when `params.maxSlippage == 0` (A...8.1.2, A...8.2.2, A...8.3.2), `UniswapV3Lib/zero-twap-seconds` when `twapSecondsAgo == 0` (A...9.1.2, A...9.2.2), and `UniswapV3Lib/min-amount-not-set` when `minAmountOut == 0` (A...9.1.2).

Each is a fail-closed default. The natural implementation shortcut — treat an unset `maxSlippage` as "no slippage constraint" — would silently make the least-configured pool the least protected one, exactly inverting the risk gradient you want. Reverting instead means a zero value can never be mistaken for a permissive value.

Operationally this splits pool enablement into two independent acts: making a pool reachable, and giving it parameters. A pool that has been added but not parameterised cannot be used at all, so a partially-completed governance change degrades into inaction rather than into unbounded exposure.

It also makes zero unusable as a legitimate setting, which is the accepted cost: there is no way to express "this pool intentionally has no slippage bound", and that is the point.
description: max-slippage-not-set, zero-twap-seconds and min-amount-not-set make governance parameterisation a precondition of use, so whitelisting a pool is not by itself enough to trade it.
